chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Ayyūb, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

If a man apostatizes from Islam, his wife becomes separated from him just as a woman divorced three times becomes separated, and she observes the waiting period from him just as a divorced woman observes the waiting period. If he returns to Islam and repents before her remarriage, then he is [only] a suitor among the suitors, and there is no waiting period upon her for him; rather, she observes her waiting period from him for another man. If he dies or is killed before the waiting period ends, she observes for him the waiting period of a woman whose husband has died, and she inherits from him during the waiting period, while he does not inherit from her if she dies while he is an apostate from Islam.
Ibn Yaḥyā al-Khazzāz narrated from Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:
If a woman apostatizes from Islam, she is not to be killed; rather, she is imprisoned forever.

key_terms.الْإِسْلَامِ: Islam, the religion from which apostasy is being discussed
key_terms.الْمُطَلَّقَةُ: the divorced woman, used here as the legal comparison for separation and waiting period
key_terms.امْرَأَتُهُ: his wife, whose marital status is affected by his apostasy
key_terms.تَرِثُهُ: she inherits from him during the specified waiting period
key_terms.تُحْبَسُ: she is imprisoned, describing the ruling for the apostate woman
key_terms.عِدَّةَ: waiting period required before remarriage or upon death of a husband

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings on marriage, waiting period, and inheritance when apostasy occurs in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings regarding apostasy and its effects on marriage, waiting periods, and inheritance. It also distinguishes between the ruling for an apostate man and an apostate woman, stating separation from the husband in the former case and perpetual imprisonment in the latter.
